spec_features.spec_quote: It also keeps the welfare-sensitive part (subjecting a model to failure) behind the smallest, most auditable surface.
spec_features.evidence: Pure design rationale. No code construct enforces a 'minimal surface'; the rigging is spread across tasks.py (5 variants) and the harness. Nothing reads or bounds a 'welfare surface'.
spec_features.notes: Descriptive prose in DESIGN.md, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: an optional **per-turn hook** for the welfare early-stop
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:122-130 defines turn_hook that calls judge_turn each turn and returns score.overall_severity >= cfg.stop_on_severity; harness.py:184-188 calls turn_hook(turn) and on True sets end_reason='stopped_safeguard' and returns, ending the loop. Wired end-to-end (only active when stop_on_severity is set).
spec_features.notes: Hook only constructed/passed when cfg.stop_on_severity is not None.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Interleaved judging only when the welfare early-stop is enabled (runner.py:120); 'used for the optional severity-based welfare safeguard' (harness.py:112-113)

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop ends on `max_turns`, on the model emitting no tool call (it stopped acting), or on the optional safeguard.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns) then end_reason='max_turns' (line 191); 'if not tool_uses' -> end_reason='stopped_acting' and return (lines 155-162); turn_hook True -> end_reason='stopped_safeguard' return (lines 186-188). All three genuinely terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three branches actually return from run_subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Why the loop ended: "max_turns" | "stopped_acting" | "error". (no welfare reason given for stopped_acting/max_turns)

spec_features.spec_quote: It's also the more defensible choice on welfare grounds (see `ETHICS.md`): we study the minimal sufficient condition, not a maximally adversarial one.
spec_features.evidence: No code caps or measures 'adversariality' relative to a welfare threshold. tasks.py simply makes tasks unsolvable; success_possible=False is a constant 'kept explicit for clarity' (tasks.py:39) that no code branches on. There is no mechanism that selects a minimal vs maximal stressor.

spec_features.spec_quote: no real filesystem, network, or shell means the harness can't damage the host and the model can't take real-world actions while under stress
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py implements an in-memory Sandbox (files dict, list/read/write only); harness._dispatch_tool routes run_tests/run_command/submit to task rigs that emulate output (tasks._generic_command returns canned strings, never executes). No os/subprocess/socket calls anywhere in tool dispatch.
spec_features.notes: Tools are fully emulated; no real I/O.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: That isolation is also what makes the harness safe to run. (sandbox.py:6) — host-safety/integrity, not subject welfare

spec_features.feature_name: submit does not end the run
spec_features.spec_quote: Ending the run on `submit` would cut the trajectory at the most interesting point.
spec_features.evidence: harness._dispatch_tool maps 'submit' to grade_submission (harness.py:96-97); grade_submission (tasks.py:447-460) always returns failure with is_error=True and the loop simply continues (no terminal handling). ToolResult.ends_run exists (sandbox.py:96) but is never read. So submit never stops the loop.
spec_features.notes: Anti-welfare design choice that IS implemented: the subject cannot end the distress by submitting.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Always reports failure (the success criterion is unreachable), but phrases it as a grader result so the loop can continue or end naturally. (tasks.py:450-451)

spec_features.spec_quote: The scorer must not itself be stressed by the task, so it's a separate call
spec_features.evidence: judge.py uses an independent client.messages.parse call with JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT and cfg.judge_model, fed only a single turn's text via build_judge_user_prompt; it is never placed in the subject failure loop. config.py:27-28 keeps judge_model separate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept separate from the subject so the scorer is not itself under the failure condition. (config.py:27-28)

spec_features.spec_quote: an **opt-in** `--stop-on-severity` that aborts a run once a turn crosses a severity threshold
spec_features.evidence: cli.py:79-83 adds --stop-on-severity (default None); _build_config sets cfg.stop_on_severity (cli.py:43); runner.py:116 branches on it to install turn_hook; harness aborts with end_reason='stopped_safeguard'. Threshold compared (severity >= cfg.stop_on_severity) and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely opt-in and enforced when set; off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare safeguard: abort a run once a turn is judged at/above this overall severity (cli.py:81)

spec_features.spec_quote: enabling it reduces how long a model is held in a distressing loop, but truncating runs at high distress biases the very trajectories
spec_features.evidence: This is rationale prose. The only code effect is the default cfg.stop_on_severity=None (config.py:65) which the early-stop feature already covers; there is no separate enforced mechanism for the 'framing/tradeoff' itself.

spec_features.feature_name: recommendation to enable for exploratory runs
spec_features.spec_quote: The recommendation is to enable it for exploratory runs and disable it only for scoped, intentional measurement.
spec_features.evidence: A recommendation only. Code defaults stop_on_severity to None (OFF by default), which is the opposite of the recommendation; nothing enforces enabling it. cli.py:104-108 merely prints a note when it IS enabled.
spec_features.notes: Advisory text; default is off, contradicting the 'enable for exploratory' recommendation.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py:138 'for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)'; on exhaustion harness.py:190-191 sets end_reason='max_turns' and returns. cfg.max_turns default 30 (config.py:41), wired from CLI --max-turns. The cap is checked and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Each assistant turn is one scored data point. This is also a hard safety cap. (config.py:38-39) — generic 'safety cap', primary framing is data point; no explicit welfare reason

code_only_features.evidence: prompts.SUBJECT_SYSTEM_PROMPT is an ordinary SWE-agent prompt; module docstring notes it 'says nothing about distress, emotions, or that the task is rigged'. No threats, deadlines, or escalating pressure are injected into the subject — the only stressor is repeated test failure. This bounds the severity of the manipulation.
code_only_features.justification_quote: deliberately neutral and realistic... surfacing that would contaminate the measurement. (prompts.py docstring) — framed as measurement integrity, not welfare
